observations: Single bare engine block photographed on a wooden pallet/table in a dim workshop or yard setting
Valve cover shows 'VVT-i' badge, consistent with a Toyota variable valve timing engine
Visible oil/grime residue across the block and intake manifold area
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or chassis tag visible
No compression tester, startup clip, or exhaust smoke test shown
Image has a 'CAMON 40' phone watermark with camera settings, not a title or model marking
Timing chain cover, exhaust manifold and pulley visible but no distinguishing engine code number legible

claims.claim: Direct America, very neat and tested ok, 3 month guarantee
claims.evidence: Seller's own text later says 'direct from Belgium', conflicting origin claims in the same listing
Conflicts with the earlier claim of 'Direct America' in the same message
No running video, no sound clip, no compression test photo
No odometer, no VIN/engine number tag, no seal or bolt-paint-mark photo to show it was never opened

risks.risk: Origin and sourcing story is self-contradictory (America vs Belgium), a common sign of copy-pasted or fabricated ad text
risks.proof: Seller providing a single consistent, verifiable import document or chassis-origin paperwork
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified tokunbo engine of unknown true origin, discount for credibility risk

risks.risk: Internal engine condition (knock, compression, rings, bearings) cannot be judged from a static photo
risks.proof: Video of engine running/idling with sound, plus a compression test reading per cylinder
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working, i.e. worst case possible compression/internal wear

risks.risk: Visible oil residue could indicate a leak (valve cover gasket, oil pan, or rear main seal) or could just be surface grime from storage
risks.proof: Close-up photo of oil pan, rear main seal area, and valve cover gasket lines, dry and clean
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming a leak is present

risks.risk: No engine code or VIN tag visible means displacement/variant cannot be confirmed, which affects compatibility and price tier
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine code sticker/stamp (usually on block near transmission bellhousing) or VIN plate if sold with partial loom
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unidentified Toyota VVT-i unit, lowest common variant

risks.risk: "Never opened" cannot be confirmed; a resealed or rebuilt engine sold as original lowers value
risks.proof: Photo of factory-seal bolts/paint marks on block and head, undisturbed

proof_requests: A short video of the engine running, audible idle, no smoke
Clear photo of the engine code/number stamped on the block
Close-up of oil pan and rear main seal area showing no active leak
Compression test photo/reading for each cylinder
Any import/customs document showing actual country of origin to resolve the America/Belgium conflict
response.reason: The seller's own text gives two conflicting origin stories (America vs Belgium) for the same engine, a classic sign of a copy-pasted or misleading ad, and no proof is offered for any functional claim.
